reviews.review:
Having put almost 300 hours into the game, I can definitely recommend it. After a lot of bland and totally not interesting releases that you'd put on a shelf after 50 hours or so, DRG feels like a breath of fresh air. But is it [i] really [/i] that good? 

The short answer? Yes. Yes it is. 

It's mind boggling that this was actually the least voted project back when Ghost Ship presented three early concepts for a video game. Looking at the game state today, one can only be proud of the development team. 

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

As for the gameplay itself, Deep Rock Galactic has some elements from the already existing games like Left 4 Dead, PayDay and Minecraft, which the game combines in the most fun way to play. On one hand, you have a horde shooter - during each mission you will be defending against hordes of bugs which have different types as well. On the other hand you have a fully destructible, randomly generated caves full of different goodies which you will be mining with your pickaxe. Objectives vary depending on the mission type, sometimes you get to eliminate dreadnoughts, sabotage rival tech, mine certain amounts of resources, and so on. 
The game has four classes to choose from - Scout, Gunner, Engineer and Driller. Each class has it's own equipment which contributes to the team. For Scout, this is flare gun to illuminate the caves and move quick with a grappling hook, Gunner has a zip-line and a dome shield which protects teammates, Engineer gets to place automated turrets and platforms, while Driller gets drills and C4 charges to destroy terrain with. 
Each class currently has 3 primary weapons and 2 secondary ones (we'll be getting third secondary weapons in the Season 2 update) which you'll be unlocking as you play the game. 
You can also customize your class how you see fit, with different perks that you unlock by playing the game.

[h1] Endgame content [/h1]

Deep Rock also has endgame content to offer, when you will reach level 25, you will be able to promote your dwarf, which drops you back to level 1, without losing any upgrades/perks you've accumulated. You will get access to Deep Dives, missions that consist of three stages, starring several main objectives. These also have an Elite counterpart and are way harder.
You might also randomly encounter an event in a regular mission, which is a mini-challenge that you might complete in order to get rewarded. 
Deep Dives give you a blank matrix core, weapon overclock and a cosmetic item, while random events let you choose your reward by spending blank matrix cores.

[h1] Community [/h1]

The community in this game is very friendly, I haven't met a single toxic person in my 289 hours of playing the game. However, I'd recommend to avoid any lobbies which only allow certain level dwarves, as they're trying to optimize everything and you'll most likely get kicked if they don't like you being slow. 

[h1] Current state [/h1]

Deep Rock Galactic gets regular updates with new content such as mission types, weapons and cosmetics. It currently has a battle-pass which is [u] completely free [/u], having lots of different cosmetic items to choose from, and it will only get bigger in Season 2 update as far as I can tell. The only paid content the game has right now is DLC packs with weapon and dwarf customization skins, but that's mostly to show your support to the developers, if you wish. 

[h1] Closing thoughts [/h1]

Deep Rock Galactic is an extremely fun cooperative game. If you longed for a game to play with your friends for hours on end - this is it. This is that game. Ghost Ship put a lot of time and effort to make one of the greatest co-op shooters out there. 

Will happily sink another 200 hours for this game several times.

[b] Rock and Stone. [/b]
